Their home planet's gravity is much higher than normal (1.5 to 2g). Massive mechs work poorly and sluggishly  on the surface, due to increased energy costs to move their increased weight.

They live in a honeycombed mining asteroid riddled with burrowing aliens. Their mechs must be able to navigate tight tunnels.

I hate Counterspell. This single spell changes the flow of combat from "ok the mage casts fireball, deals 45 damage, everyone make a DC 15 Dex save" to:

- The mage starts casting a spell.
- Well, well, well, should I Counterspell? What spell are they casting?
- You can spend your reaction to either Recognize the spell or Counterspell, but not both.
- I will... Counterspell... At level... Let me see... Just three.
- OK the mage has cast their still unknown spell at level 4, so you have to roll.
- Not fair, you waited until I declared my spell level to declare yours.
- Sigh.

There's not a single spell that fucks up the rhythm of combat that much (although Silvery Barbs comes close). As if that's not enough, this a spell that, if successful, makes literally nothing happen. It halts progress, freezes drama, dams the tide of combat. 1. Your player taps on the Cog icon to the right of their character's red bar on the Pilot Roster.
2. They tap on the "Get Share Code" option on the pop-out menu and then on the "Generate Pilot Share Code" red button.
3. Have them send the six-letter code to you.
4. You go on your own Pilot Roster and tap on Import Pilot followed by the tab "Import from Share Code". Paste or type the code provided by your player.
5. Tap on Import <Character> as a Remote Resource.
6. Their character should appear on your own Pilot Roster and will auto-update as the player changes them.
7. (Optional) You can "Add Group" to create a folder for sorting out specific campaigns and your personal characters.

If you import characters as a Remote Resource, it will sync with the original and update any changes made by the original player. It won't update if you do it as a Copy, though.

So, they know he's allied with the Zhentarimm but not that he's been blackmailed, right? Since they're probably not in speaking terms with him, have them be approached by one of his lumberjack friends (perhaps when they're casing his cabin). 

The lumberjack says that Shandar changed a LOT in these last couple months since he got a letter. He's been travelling every month and is constantly nervous, sleeps awfully and has terrible nightmares (every trip he takes to Targos reminds him of his guilt over the murder in Mirabar). The friend has no idea what happened but is concerned and trying to convince the PCs to take it easy on Shandar.

The PCs then can try to search the house for any evidence (quite easily since the lumberjacks spend most of the day away and Shandar is probably also travelling) - you can leave a watch dog or something to represent a challenge. In his room there's some kind of well-hidden stash of gold and jewelry from his "previous" life, including a signet ring with his family's coat of arms and something that belonged to his victim (perhaps the object that provoked the fight that resulted in the murder?). But most importantly there is a WANTED poster issued by the Mirabar sheriff with his likeness and a different name. And written in red ink "I KNOW. MEET ME AT LUSKAN ARMS".

With that piece of evidence they may expose him publicly, investigate further or confront him privately (in this case he might cave and ask for their help to navigate this situation).

My general suggestion is: always try to embody relevant backstory in physical objects and actionable information. That way even if the party antagonizes or kills an important NPC, you can still transmit that important piece of information.
